title: Some unconventional problems in number theory
relevance: Original problem and finite logarithmic lower bound, printed page 77.
reviewed_sections: Complete ten-page extracted text read in the immediately preceding audit
Printed page 77 visually checked in that audit and reused here
proof_checked_sections: The elementary logarithmic lower-bound argument, with non-strict inequality and explicit domain
review_note: Full extracted-text reading is reused, not a claim of a new complete visual rereading. The strict displayed > needs correction to >= on the stated general finite domain. The main asymptotic problem is not proved.

applications.hypothesis_check: Current candidate theorem assumes natural 0<k<n, hence n>1 and a positive binomial coefficient.
applications.bridge: Kummer bounds each full prime-power component by n; multiply over distinct primes, take logs and divide by positive log n.

title: Asymptotics for smooth numbers in short intervals
relevance: Theorem 1.1 supplies a valid analytic input for the upper pointwise subrange.
review_note: Only the first three pages were read, not the full 30-page proof. Exact primary theorem statement and parameter range were checked. CC BY 4.0 in arXiv record.

applications.hypothesis_check: For fixed delta and nonempty range choose theta=17/30+delta/2, x=n-k,h=k,y=k. Hypotheses hold uniformly eventually.
applications.bridge: At k^2>=n the large-prime count is the count of non-k-smooth interval terms. Global floors, Chebyshev and Mertens give the reciprocal-prime main term. This is an informal derived corollary, not implemented by the finite lower-bound candidate.

title: Erdos Problem #685 at Density One: An Unconditional Proof of the Erdos-Gupta-Khare Second-Moment Conjecture
relevance: Distinguishes density-one and second-moment claims from the open pointwise conjecture.
reviewed_sections: Selected Lean statement and proof excerpts
review_note: Not the entire paper or Lean dependency closure. No rebuild. Principal claims use custom mathematical axioms for Mertens, Turan-Kubilius and Matomaki-Radziwill. Main pointwise problem explicitly remains open. No license detected. Not imported.

title: On the number of distinct prime divisors of the binomial coefficient (n choose k)
relevance: Original first-moment theorem and second-moment conjecture cited by Weatherhead.
review_note: Utilitas Mathematica 10 (1976),51-60; only the Weatherhead bibliography entry inspected. Original source was not retrieved or read; not screened as a primary paper.

title: Binomial Coefficients and the Distribution of the Primes
relevance: Known fixed-ratio binomial distinct-prime asymptotic; source parameters 2,1 give the proposed central-binomial formalization.
reviewed_sections: 3 The Lemma and the Three Theorems, including all proofs and remarks
4 Applications, including all three corollaries, proofs and remarks
review_note: Entire primary HTML read, including substantive equations, corresponding to 15-page v1. Full-paper reading is distinct from certification of every proof. Theorem2 is explicitly attributed by Xylouris to Erdos1979 p77. Fixed-factor omission in small-prime bound is asymptotically harmless; formalization uses corrected finite bound. Original 1979 theorem is not new mathematics. No claim that bibliography works were read.

applications.source_result: Theorem 2 with fixed source parameters 2 and 1
applications.hypothesis_check: The fixed integers satisfy 2>1>0; the source scale tends to infinity through naturals.
applications.bridge: The source coefficient is log(2^2/(1^1*1^1))=log4. Its asymptotic is exactly the normalized central limit. The implementation uses a logarithmic cutoff and elementary central-binomial bounds.
